```{r setup}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What to set for a report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The path to the config file, whose secfiling section names the Silver layer
# of the module. A chunk runs with the directory of this template as its
# working directory, which is inside the installed package, so the path is
# taken from the environment variable FINCOMMONS_CONFIG where it is set and
# is otherwise a paths.yaml beside the template.
config_path <- Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_CONFIG", "paths.yaml")

# The registrants the report covers, by central index key, zero-padded to
# ten digits as the company files write them, or NULL for every registrant
# the lake holds.
report_ciks <- NULL

# The years shown, by the year the filing was made, or NULL for the last
# `n_years` the lake holds. The year a filing was made is the partition
# column of both tables and is monotonic; the fiscal year is not, a
# registrant that moves its year end reporting two of them or none.
report_years <- NULL
n_years <- 6

# How many rows the rankings of filings and registrants show.
top_n <- 15

# The point size of the text in a chart.
chart_base_size <- 9

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What each check is asked of
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The catalogue of checks says what a code means; it does not say which
# filings the check could have fired on, and a share is only readable
# against the right denominator. A check that reads a balance sheet can only
# fire on a filing that carries one, and a 10-Q that states no annual
# figures is not a filing that passed those checks.
#
#   "filed"  -- every filing the table of filings holds, of the forms the
#               run collected.
#   "annual" -- the filings made on one of the annual forms, amendment or
#               not, which are the ones that carry a full set of
#               statements.
#
# Every code of the catalogue has to appear here, or the report stops: a
# check added to the module and not to this list would otherwise be counted
# against whichever denominator happened to be lying around.
populations <- tibble::tribble(
  ~code,                          ~population,
  "IMBAL_BALANCE_SHEET",          "annual",
  "IMBAL_TOTALS",                 "annual",
  "IMBAL_INCOME",                 "annual",
  "IMBAL_PROFIT",                 "annual",
  "IMBAL_CASHFLOW",               "annual",
  "IMPL_NEGATIVE_ASSETS",         "annual",
  "MISS_ASSETS",                  "annual",
  "MISS_REVENUE",                 "annual",
  "MISS_PROFIT",                  "annual",
  "RESTATED_MATERIALLY",          "annual",
  "IMPL_PERIOD",                  "filed",
  "IMPL_FILED_BEFORE_PERIODEND",  "filed",
  "IMPL_FY_PERIODEND",            "filed",
  "DUPL_FACT_VALUE",              "filed",
  "MIXED_UNIT",                   "filed",
  "MISS_FRAMEWORK",               "filed")

# The forms that carry a full set of annual statements, amendment or not.
# The same list the module checks against, and a change to one without the
# other would put the shares of this report against the wrong population.
annual_forms <- c("10-K", "20-F", "40-F")

# The order the severities are read in, from the one that stops an analysis
# to the one that only describes it.
severities <- c("error", "warning", "info")

# What a row of the table of issues is about, which is what makes the two
# counts of this report different things. A check names the records that
# failed it: a filing, where the fault is a fault of the filing as a whole,
# and a fact, where one figure of it is at fault. So a code that names facts
# has as many rows for one filing as that filing has bad facts.
#
#   findings -- rows of the table of issues.
#   affected -- distinct filings named by those rows.
#
# No table in this report adds a count of findings to a count of filings.

# You can adapt your corporate design in the sourced R-Skript. It is one file
# for the whole package, in the templates directory beside the modules, so
# that a report of either regime looks like the other and a change to the
# design is made once rather than once per module. A copy beside this
# template wins over it, which is what lets a template taken out of the
# package carry a design of its own.
library(ggplot2)
design_file <- "r-corporate-design-functions-ggplot2.R"
design_path <- c(design_file, file.path("..", "..", "templates", design_file))
design_path <- design_path[file.exists(design_path)]
if (length(design_path) == 0) {
  stop("The corporate design script ", design_file, " is neither beside this ",
       "template nor in the templates directory of the package.")
}
source(design_path[1])

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(yaml)
library(arrow)

# The form a filing was made on, without the amendment suffix: a 10-K/A is
# an amended annual report and carries the statements of one.
base_form <- function(form) sub("/.*$", "", form)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The catalogue of checks
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The same file the module reads, so that the report describes the checks
# that ran rather than a copy of their descriptions that has drifted. It
# lives in the data directory of the package; a copy beside this template
# wins over it, as the design script does.
catalogue_file <- "dataquality_checks.csv"
catalogue_path <- c(catalogue_file,
                    file.path("..", "..", "data", catalogue_file))
catalogue_path <- catalogue_path[file.exists(catalogue_path)]
if (length(catalogue_path) == 0) {
  stop("The catalogue of checks ", catalogue_file, " is neither beside this ",
       "template nor in the data directory of the package.")
}

catalogue <- read.csv(catalogue_path[1], stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  filter(dataset == "secfiling") %>%
  as_tibble()

if (nrow(catalogue) == 0) {
  stop("The catalogue of checks names no check of the secfiling module.")
}

undeclared <- setdiff(catalogue$code, populations$code)
if (length(undeclared) > 0) {
  stop("The catalogue names checks this template does not know the ",
       "population of: ", paste(undeclared, collapse = ", "),
       ". Add them to `populations` in the settings of this template.")
}

unknown_severity <- setdiff(catalogue$severity, severities)
if (length(unknown_severity) > 0) {
  stop("The catalogue uses severities this template does not order: ",
       paste(unknown_severity, collapse = ", "), ".")
}

catalogue <- catalogue %>%
  left_join(populations, by = "code") %>%
  mutate(severity = factor(severity, levels = severities)) %>%
  arrange(severity, code)

n_checks <- nrow(catalogue)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Silver layer
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

yaml_paths <- read_yaml(config_path)
path_silver <- yaml_paths[["secfiling"]][["silver"]]

# The Silver layer may name a schema in a catalogue rather than a directory,
# with the directory the tables are written to beside it. R reads files, so
# it takes the directory.
if (is.list(path_silver)) path_silver <- path_silver[["path"]]

# arrow reads every parquet file under a directory. A Delta table keeps the
# files it has replaced until it is vacuumed, and both of these tables are
# written a partition at a time, so a Delta table read this way counts a row
# once for every time it was written. This report counts rows, so it refuses
# one rather than show those counts.
for (table in c("filings", "issues")) {
  if (dir.exists(file.path(path_silver, table, "_delta_log"))) {
    stop("The ", table, " table of the secfiling module is a Delta table, ",
         "which this template does not read. Write the Silver layer as ",
         "parquet, or read the table through Spark.")
  }
}

if (!dir.exists(file.path(path_silver, "issues"))) {
  stop("The secfiling module has no table of issues in ", path_silver,
       ". Run the checks first: python -c \"from pyspark.sql import ",
       "SparkSession; from fincommons.secfiling.quality import ",
       "update_silver_secfiling_quality; update_silver_secfiling_quality(",
       "SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate(), '<paths.yaml>')\"")
}

filings_all <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "filings")) %>%
  select(CIK, FILING, NAME, FORM, FP, FY, FILED, PERIODEND, FACTS,
         FRAMEWORK) %>%
  collect()

if (nrow(filings_all) == 0) {
  stop("The table of filings of the secfiling module is empty. Run the ",
       "pipeline first: python -m fincommons.secfiling --config ",
       "<paths.yaml> --cik 0001045810 --contact <you@example.org>")
}

issues_all <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "issues")) %>% collect()

if (nrow(issues_all) == 0) {
  stop("The table of issues of the secfiling module is empty. Either the ",
       "checks have not run over any registrant yet, or the Silver layer ",
       "holds no filing at all.")
}

# The partition column comes from the directory name when the table is
# written partitioned and from the file when it is not, and arrow reads the
# two as different types. One type here, so the joins below hold either way.
issues_all <- issues_all %>%
  mutate(across(c(CIK, FILING, ISSUE), as.character),
         FILEDYEAR = as.integer(FILEDYEAR),
         CHECKED = as.Date(CHECKED))

# The table of filings carries no year of its own: the year filed is the
# partition column of the facts and of the issues, and it is derived there
# from FILED. Derived the same way here, or the join below would miss.
filings_all <- filings_all %>%
  mutate(CIK = as.character(CIK),
         FILING = as.character(FILING),
         FILEDYEAR = as.integer(format(FILED, "%Y")),
         annual = base_form(FORM) %in% annual_forms)

# A code in the table that the catalogue does not describe is a check that
# was removed or renamed and whose rows were left behind. The report cannot
# say what it means, so it stops rather than print a bare code.
uncatalogued <- setdiff(unique(issues_all$ISSUE), catalogue$code)
if (length(uncatalogued) > 0) {
  stop("The table of issues holds codes the catalogue does not describe: ",
       paste(uncatalogued, collapse = ", "), ". Run the checks again, which ",
       "rewrites the partitions it checks as a whole.")
}

# The registrants and the years the report covers. A registrant named in the
# settings that the table does not list is an error rather than an empty
# column, because a report that silently covers less than it says is worse
# than one that does not render.
ciks_held <- sort(unique(filings_all$CIK))
if (is.null(report_ciks)) {
  report_ciks <- ciks_held
} else {
  report_ciks <- formatC(gsub("[^0-9]", "", report_ciks), width = 10,
                         flag = "0")
  unknown <- setdiff(report_ciks, ciks_held)
  if (length(unknown) > 0) {
    stop("The table of filings lists no filing of ",
         paste(unknown, collapse = ", "), ".")
  }
}

years_held <- sort(unique(filings_all$FILEDYEAR[!is.na(filings_all$FILEDYEAR)]))
if (is.null(report_years)) {
  report_years <- tail(years_held, n_years)
} else {
  unknown <- setdiff(report_years, years_held)
  if (length(unknown) > 0) {
    stop("The table of filings lists no filing made in ",
         paste(unknown, collapse = ", "), ".")
  }
}
report_years <- sort(as.integer(report_years))
year_labels <- as.character(report_years)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The record the checks were asked about
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Every filing of the selection, of every form the run collected. A quality
# report counts what was checked, and an amended filing was checked like the
# one it amends; the factsheet in this directory is the one that picks a
# filing per period.
filings <- filings_all %>%
  filter(CIK %in% report_ciks, FILEDYEAR %in% report_years) %>%
  rename(fy = FILEDYEAR)

if (nrow(filings) == 0) {
  stop("No filing of the table falls in the registrants and years of this ",
       "report.")
}

# A partition of the table of filings with no row in the table of issues is
# either a partition every check passed or a partition no check has run
# over. Nothing in the two tables tells the two apart, so the report names
# the years it cannot speak for rather than count them as sound.
checked_years <- sort(unique(issues_all$FILEDYEAR))
silent_years <- setdiff(report_years, checked_years)

issues <- issues_all %>%
  rename(fy = FILEDYEAR) %>%
  inner_join(filings %>% select(CIK, fy, FILING, NAME, FORM, PERIODEND,
                                FILED, annual),
             by = c("CIK", "fy", "FILING")) %>%
  left_join(catalogue %>% select(ISSUE = code, severity, title, population),
            by = "ISSUE")

# An issue row whose filing the table of filings does not list is a row left
# over from a filing the Commission no longer carries in the company file.
# It cannot be placed in a form or a registrant, so it is counted and set
# aside.
orphans <- issues_all %>%
  rename(fy = FILEDYEAR) %>%
  anti_join(filings_all %>% rename(fy = FILEDYEAR) %>%
              select(CIK, fy, FILING),
            by = c("CIK", "fy", "FILING"))

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What the checks found
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The two populations, and which of them the rates of this report are
# taken over.
#
# A check asked of every filing was also asked of every annual report, the
# one population being inside the other, so the annual reports are the only
# population every check of the module was asked about. The rates of this
# report -- the share free of errors, the shares by year and by registrant,
# the bands of findings per filing -- are therefore taken over those, and a
# quarterly filing is counted only in the checks asked of every filing.
# Taken over every filing instead, a record of which the quarterly reports
# are the bulk would read as sound because the checks that read a balance
# sheet had never looked at them.
n_filed <- nrow(filings)
n_annual <- sum(filings$annual)

# One row per code: the rows it wrote, the filings those rows name, and that
# count against the filings the check could have fired on at all.
by_code <- issues %>%
  group_by(ISSUE) %>%
  summarise(findings = n(),
            affected = n_distinct(FILING),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  right_join(catalogue %>% select(ISSUE = code, severity, title, population),
             by = "ISSUE") %>%
  mutate(findings = coalesce(findings, 0L),
         affected = coalesce(affected, 0L),
         denominator = ifelse(population == "annual", n_annual, n_filed),
         share = ifelse(denominator > 0, affected / denominator * 100,
                        NA_real_)) %>%
  arrange(severity, desc(affected), ISSUE)

# One row per filing the checks named, with the severity of the worst thing
# found in it. A filing with no row here is one every check passed -- which,
# for a year no check has run over, is a statement this report does not
# make.
per_filing <- issues %>%
  group_by(CIK, fy, FILING) %>%
  summarise(findings = n(),
            codes = n_distinct(ISSUE),
            errors = sum(severity == "error"),
            warnings = sum(severity == "warning"),
            infos = sum(severity == "info"),
            worst = severities[min(as.integer(severity))],
            which = paste(sort(unique(ISSUE)), collapse = ", "),
            .groups = "drop")

# Every filing of the selection, with a zero where no check named it.
filing_state <- filings %>%
  select(CIK, fy, FILING, NAME, FORM, FP, PERIODEND, FILED, FACTS,
         FRAMEWORK, annual) %>%
  left_join(per_filing, by = c("CIK", "fy", "FILING")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(findings, codes, errors, warnings, infos),
                ~ coalesce(.x, 0L)),
         worst = coalesce(worst, "none"),
         which = coalesce(which, ""),
         clean = errors == 0,
         spotless = findings == 0)

# The filings every check was asked of, which is what every rate below is
# taken over.
rated <- filing_state %>% filter(annual)

if (nrow(rated) == 0) {
  stop("No filing of this selection was made on one of the annual forms (",
       paste(annual_forms, collapse = ", "), "), so no check that reads a ",
       "set of statements could have run. Widen the years, or collect a ",
       "registrant that files an annual report.")
}

# Per year filed: the record checked, and how much of the annual part of it
# carries an error or carries nothing at all.
by_year <- filing_state %>%
  group_by(fy) %>%
  summarise(filed = n(),
            annual = sum(annual),
            registrants = n_distinct(CIK),
            findings = sum(findings),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(rated %>%
              group_by(fy) %>%
              summarise(with_error = sum(errors > 0),
                        clean = sum(clean) / n() * 100,
                        spotless = sum(spotless) / n() * 100,
                        error_share = sum(errors > 0) / n() * 100,
                        warning_share = sum(warnings > 0) / n() * 100,
                        info_share = sum(infos > 0) / n() * 100,
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = "fy")

by_form <- filing_state %>%
  mutate(form = base_form(FORM)) %>%
  group_by(form) %>%
  summarise(filed = n(),
            findings = sum(findings),
            per_filing = sum(findings) / n(),
            with_error = sum(errors > 0),
            error_share = sum(errors > 0) / n() * 100,
            clean = sum(clean) / n() * 100,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(filed), form)

by_registrant <- filing_state %>%
  group_by(CIK, NAME) %>%
  summarise(filed = n(),
            annual = sum(annual),
            findings = sum(findings),
            errors = sum(errors),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(rated %>%
              group_by(CIK) %>%
              summarise(clean = sum(clean) / n() * 100, .groups = "drop"),
            by = "CIK") %>%
  arrange(desc(errors), desc(findings))

# The five identities, which are the checks that say the figures of an
# annual report are consistent with one another. They are grouped because an
# analysis that reads a statement out of a filing rests on all five at once.
identity_codes <- catalogue$code[grepl("^IMBAL_", catalogue$code)]
identity_state <- rated %>%
  left_join(issues %>%
              filter(ISSUE %in% identity_codes) %>%
              distinct(CIK, fy, FILING) %>%
              mutate(fails_identity = TRUE),
            by = c("CIK", "fy", "FILING")) %>%
  mutate(fails_identity = coalesce(fails_identity, FALSE))

checked_on <- range(issues_all$CHECKED)
```

```{r formats}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Writing numbers and words
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  x <- ifelse(!is.na(x) & abs(x) < 0.5 / 10^digits, 0, x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "–",
         formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",",
                 decimal.mark = "."))
}

wrap_caption <- function(text, width = 125) {
  paste(strwrap(text, width = width), collapse = "\n")
}

max_date <- max(filings$FILED, na.rm = TRUE)
period_range <- paste0(min(report_years), " – ", max(report_years))

source_caption <- caption_corporate_design(
  source = paste("Company facts of the U.S. Securities and Exchange",
                 "Commission; checks of the fincommons secfiling module."),
  last = format(max(checked_on), "%d %b %Y"),
  lang = "en")

typst_string <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\\\\", "\\\\\\\\", x)
  gsub("\"", "\\\\\"", x)
}

severity_label <- function(x) {
  recode(as.character(x), error = "Error", warning = "Warning",
         info = "Note", none = "Nothing found")
}

# A table of one row per item and one column per year filed.
render_years <- function(data, value, digits = 0, label_column = "label",
                         header = "", order = NULL) {
  wide <- data %>%
    mutate(.v = {{ value }}) %>%
    select(all_of(label_column), fy, .v) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = "fy", values_from = ".v")
  if (!is.null(order)) {
    wide <- wide[match(order, wide[[label_column]]), ]
    wide[[label_column]] <- order
  }
  out <- tibble(item = wide[[label_column]])
  for (y in report_years) {
    column <- as.character(y)
    out[[column]] <- if (column %in% names(wide)) fmt(wide[[column]], digits)
                     else "–"
  }
  knitr::kable(out, col.names = c(header, year_labels),
               align = paste0("l", strrep("r", length(report_years))))
}

# A chart of one line per group over the years filed.
chart_by_year <- function(data, value, group, subtitle = "%", digits = 0,
                          ncol = 5, zero = TRUE) {
  d <- data %>% mutate(.v = {{ value }}, .g = {{ group }}) %>% filter(!is.na(.v))
  g <- ggplot(d, aes(x = fy, y = .v, colour = .g)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = linewidth_corporate_design) +
    geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = report_years, labels = year_labels,
                       expand = c(.02, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) fmt(x, digits)) +
    scale_colour_corporate_design() +
    labs(caption = wrap_caption(source_caption), subtitle = subtitle) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = ncol)) +
    theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size,
                           axis.title = element_blank())
  if (zero) g <- g + geom_zeroline()
  g
}

# A chart of bars, one per category, read from top to bottom.
chart_ranked <- function(data, value, label, subtitle = "%", digits = 0,
                         wrap = 44, fill = NULL) {
  d <- data %>%
    mutate(.v = {{ value }}, .l = wrap_labels({{ label }}, wrap)) %>%
    arrange(.v) %>%
    mutate(.l = factor(.l, levels = .l))
  # `missing` and not `is.null`, because the argument is given as an
  # expression over the columns of the data and evaluating it here, outside
  # the data, is what `is.null` would do.
  g <- if (missing(fill)) {
    ggplot(d, aes(x = .v, y = .l)) +
      geom_col(fill = palette_corporate_design("cat")[1], width = 0.72)
  } else {
    d <- d %>% mutate(.f = {{ fill }})
    ggplot(d, aes(x = .v, y = .l, fill = .f)) +
      geom_col(width = 0.72) +
      scale_fill_corporate_design() +
      guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 3))
  }
  g +
    geom_zeroline(x = 0) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) fmt(x, digits),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .06))) +
    labs(caption = wrap_caption(source_caption), subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size, grid = "x",
                           axis.title = element_blank())
}
```

```{r cover, results='asis'}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The cover and the running head
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

ts <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) x <- "–"
  paste0("\"", typst_string(as.character(x)), "\"")
}

typst_kv <- function(items) {
  rows <- vapply(seq_along(items), function(i) {
    paste0("  text(size: 7.5pt, fill: soft, ", ts(names(items)[i]), "),\n",
           "  text(size: 8.5pt, ", ts(items[[i]]), "),")
  }, character(1))
  paste0("#grid(columns: (3.5cm, 1fr), row-gutter: 5.5pt, column-gutter: 6pt,\n",
         paste(rows, collapse = "\n"), "\n)")
}

n_findings <- sum(filing_state$findings)
n_errors <- sum(by_code$findings[by_code$severity == "error"])
n_warnings <- sum(by_code$findings[by_code$severity == "warning"])
n_infos <- sum(by_code$findings[by_code$severity == "info"])
n_registrants <- n_distinct(filing_state$CIK)
share_clean <- mean(rated$clean) * 100
share_spotless <- mean(rated$spotless) * 100
share_identity <- mean(!identity_state$fails_identity) * 100

record_items <- list()
record_items[["Registrants"]] <- fmt(n_registrants)
record_items[["Years filed"]] <- period_range
record_items[["Filings checked"]] <- fmt(n_filed)
record_items[["Of those, annual"]] <- fmt(n_annual)
record_items[["Checks run"]] <- fmt(n_checks)
record_items[["Checked on"]] <-
  if (checked_on[1] == checked_on[2]) format(checked_on[1], "%d %B %Y") else
    paste(format(checked_on[1], "%d %b %Y"), "–",
          format(checked_on[2], "%d %b %Y"))

found_items <- list()
found_items[["Findings"]] <- fmt(n_findings)
found_items[["Of those, errors"]] <- fmt(n_errors)
found_items[["Annual with an error"]] <-
  paste0(fmt(sum(rated$errors > 0)), " (", fmt(100 - share_clean, 1), " %)")
found_items[["Free of errors, %"]] <- fmt(share_clean, 1)
found_items[["Nothing found at all, %"]] <- fmt(share_spotless, 1)
found_items[["Identities hold, %"]] <- fmt(share_identity, 1)

notice <- paste(
  "The checks of the `secfiling` module of fincommons, run over the company",

{{< pagebreak >}}

### How this report is built

```{r basis, results='asis'}
basis <- c(
  paste0("**What it reads.** Two Silver tables of the `secfiling` module of ",
         "fincommons: the table of filings, one row per filing the company ",
         "files name, and the table of issues, one row per record that ",
         "failed a check. The table of issues is written by ",
         "`fincommons.secfiling.quality`, which runs the ", fmt(n_checks),
         " checks of the module over the facts and the filings and writes ",
         "what they found; this report does not re-run them. The catalogue ",
         "of checks in section 5 is read from the same file the module ",
         "reads, so what a code means here is what it means there."),
  paste0("**What a finding is.** A row of the table of issues: one record ",
         "that failed one check. Where the fault belongs to the filing as a ",
         "whole -- a balance sheet that does not balance -- the record is ",
         "the filing, and there is one row. Where one figure is at fault -- ",
         "a concept tagged twice with two values -- the record is the fact, ",
         "and a filing has as many rows as it has such facts. The two ",
         "counts are therefore different things, and this report names them ",
         "apart throughout: **findings** are rows, **filings** are the ",
         "distinct filings those rows name. No table adds one to the other."),
  paste0("**What it is counted against.** A check that reads a balance ",
         "sheet can only fire on a filing that carries one. Of the ",
         fmt(n_filed), " filings in this selection, ", fmt(n_annual),
         " were made on an annual form. The share for each check in ",
         "section 2 is taken against whichever of the two populations the ",
         "check is asked of, and the population of each is in the table of ",
         "checks below; every other rate in this report -- the share free ",
         "of errors, the shares by year and by registrant, the bands of ",
         "findings per filing -- is taken over the ", fmt(n_annual),
         " annual reports, which is the one population every check of the ",
         "module was asked about. A quarterly filing is counted only in the ",
         "checks asked of every filing. Over every filing instead, a record ",
         "of which the quarterly reports are the bulk would read as sound ",
         "because the checks that read a balance sheet had never looked at ",
         "them."),
  paste0("**Why the years are the years filed.** A company file is ",
         "organised by concept and carries every filing's account of every ",
         "period, and the year a filing was made is the one column of it ",
         "that only ever moves forward. A registrant that changes its year ",
         "end reports two fiscal years or none, so a report counted by ",
         "fiscal year would gain and lose filings for a reason that has ",
         "nothing to do with their quality. The years here are therefore ",
         "the years the filings were made, which is also what both tables ",
         "are partitioned by."),
  paste0("**What a severity means.** An **error** is a finding that an ",
         "analysis cannot read past: the figures of the filing contradict ",
         "one another, or a date is impossible. A **warning** is a finding ",
         "that needs a human to look at the filing before its figures are ",
         "used. A **note** describes the filing without faulting it. The ",
         "three are this project's judgement of how much a finding costs a ",
         "reader, not a classification the Commission publishes."),
  paste0("**What it does not do.** Nothing in the module corrects a figure ",
         "or drops a filing. A check writes a row and leaves the data as it ",
         "is, which is what lets the table of issues be read beside the ",
         "figures rather than instead of them. A filing with findings is ",
         "still in the table of facts, and whether to use it is the ",
         "reader's decision to make."))

cat(paste(basis, collapse = "\n\n"))
```

  transmute(code = paste0("`", code, "`"),
            severity = severity_label(severity),
            title,
            population = recode(population,
                                filed = "Every filing",
                                annual = "Annual reports"))

knitr::kable(temp, align = "llll", col.names = c(
  "Code", "Severity", "What it finds", "Asked of"))
```

## 2 What the checks found

### The findings, by severity

```{r found-severity, results='asis'}
n_rated_findings <- sum(rated$findings)

cat("The ", fmt(n_checks), " checks wrote ", fmt(n_findings),
    " findings over the ", fmt(n_filed), " filings checked: ", fmt(n_errors),
    " errors, ", fmt(n_warnings), " warnings and ", fmt(n_infos),
    " notes. Of those, ", fmt(n_rated_findings), " fall on the ",
    fmt(n_annual), " annual reports, which is the population every check ",
    "was asked of and the one the table and the shares below are taken ",
    "over; the remaining ", fmt(n_findings - n_rated_findings),
    " fall on the other forms, where only the checks asked of every filing ",
    "could fire at all. A filing can carry findings of several severities, ",
    "so the shares do not add to a hundred.\n\n", sep = "")

if (nrow(orphans) > 0) {
  cat("\n", fmt(nrow(orphans)), " further rows of the table of issues name ",
      "filings the table of filings no longer lists, which is what a filing ",
      "the Commission dropped from a company file leaves behind. They are ",
      "counted nowhere else in this report.\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r severity-table}
# Both counts over the annual reports, which is what keeps a row of this
# table from putting findings of one population beside filings of another.
temp <- rated %>%
  summarise(across(c(errors, warnings, infos), ~ sum(.x > 0)),
            none = sum(spotless)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "severity", values_to = "filings") %>%
  mutate(label = recode(severity, errors = "An error",
                        warnings = "A warning", infos = "A note",
                        none = "Nothing at all"),
         findings = c(sum(rated$errors), sum(rated$warnings),
                      sum(rated$infos), 0),
         share = filings / n_annual * 100)

knitr::kable(temp %>% transmute(label, Findings = fmt(findings),
                                Filings = fmt(filings),
                                Share = fmt(share, 1)),
             align = "lrrr",
             col.names = c("Filings carrying", "Findings", "Annual reports",
                           "Of those, %"))
```

### How the findings fall across the record

```{r found-concentration}
# A record in which every filing carries one finding and one in which a
# tenth of the filings carry ten are the same count and are not the same
# problem. These are the bands of findings per filing.
bands <- c(0, 1, 2, 3, 6, 11, Inf)
band_labels <- c("None", "1", "2", "3 – 5", "6 – 10", "> 10")

temp <- rated %>%
  mutate(band = cut(findings, breaks = bands, labels = band_labels,
                    include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)) %>%
  count(fy, band, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  group_by(fy) %>%
  mutate(share = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(label = band)

render_years(temp, share, digits = 1,
             header = "Findings per annual report, %", order = band_labels)
```

```{r found-concentration-note, results='asis'}
top_share <- rated %>%
  arrange(desc(findings)) %>%
  slice_head(n = max(1, round(nrow(rated) / 100)))
cat("\nThe loudest one per cent of the annual reports -- ",
    fmt(nrow(top_share)), " of them -- carry ",
    fmt(sum(top_share$findings) / max(n_findings, 1) * 100, 1),
    " % of all findings. A count of findings is therefore not a measure of ",
    "how much of the record is usable; the share of filings free of errors ",
    "in section 3 is.\n", sep = "")
```

### How much of it is free of errors

```{r clean-note, results='asis'}
cat("No error was found in ", fmt(sum(rated$clean)), " of the ",
    fmt(n_annual), " annual reports checked, and nothing at all in ",
    fmt(sum(rated$spotless)), ". ",
    "The first is the share an analysis that reads figures out of these ",
    "filings can work with; the second is the share about which nothing at ",
    "all was found, which is a stricter test than most uses need -- a ",
    "warning that a later report restated a figure is a fact about the ",
    "record and not a fault in either filing.\n", sep = "")
```

### The five identities

```{r identities, results='asis'}
cat("Five of the checks test an annual report against itself: that the ",
    "balance sheet balances, that the two totals of it agree, that revenue ",
    "less the cost of revenue is the gross profit, that income before tax ",
    "less the tax is the net income, and that the three cash flows sum to ",
    "the change in cash. They are the checks an analysis that reads a ",
    "statement out of a filing rests on, and they are read together here ",
    "because a filing that fails any one of them cannot be read as a set of ",
    "statements.\n\n", sep = "")

cat("All five hold in ", fmt(sum(!identity_state$fails_identity)),
    " of the ", fmt(n_annual), " annual reports checked, ",
    fmt(share_identity, 1), " % of them.\n", sep = "")
```

```{r identities-table}
temp <- by_code %>%
  filter(ISSUE %in% identity_codes) %>%
  transmute(title,
            Filings = fmt(affected),
            Share = fmt(share, 1))

knitr::kable(temp, align = "lrr",
             col.names = c("The identity", "Annual reports failing it",
                           "Of the annual reports, %"))
```

```{r identities-silent, results='asis'}
# An identity can only be tested where the filing tags both sides of it. A
# filing that tags neither passes by silence, which is a different thing
# from passing, and the MISS_ checks are what makes that visible.
miss <- by_code %>% filter(grepl("^MISS_", ISSUE), ISSUE != "MISS_FRAMEWORK")
cat("\nAn identity is only tested where the filing tags the lines it rests ",
    "on. A filing that tags neither side of one passes it by silence, which ",
    "is not the same as passing it: ",
    paste(sprintf("%s in %s %% of the annual reports",
                  tolower(miss$title), fmt(miss$share, 1)),
          collapse = "; "),
    ". Those are the ", nrow(miss), " `MISS_` checks over the figures, and ",
    "they are what keeps a silent pass from reading as a sound report.\n",
    sep = "")
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

### What a later report says about an earlier one

```{r restatement, results='asis'}
# The one check of this module that has no counterpart in esef, and the
# reason it is here: a company file carries every filing's account of every
# period, so the figure a year's own report stated can be set beside the
# figure a later report states for the same year.
restated <- by_code %>% filter(ISSUE == "RESTATED_MATERIALLY")
restated_filings <- issues %>%
  filter(ISSUE == "RESTATED_MATERIALLY") %>%
  distinct(CIK, FILING)

cat("A company file is organised by concept and carries every filing's ",
    "account of every period, which is what makes a restatement visible at ",
    "all: the figure a year's own annual report stated can be set beside ",
    "the figure a later annual report states for the same year. The ",
    "`RESTATED_MATERIALLY` check names the facts where the two differ by ",
    "more than a hundredth. It found ", fmt(restated$findings),
    " such facts in ", fmt(nrow(restated_filings)), " filings, ",
    fmt(restated$share, 1), " % of the annual reports checked.\n\n", sep = "")

cat("A restatement, a reclassification and a correction all look the same ",
    "in the figures, and which of the three it is cannot be read from them. ",
    "Share counts and per-share amounts are passed over by the check, a ",
    "split restating those by arithmetic rather than by judgement. The ",
    "`esef` module has no counterpart to this check: the repository ",
    "publishes each filing on its own, so there is no one place that holds ",
    "two filings' accounts of one year.\n", sep = "")
```

```{r restatement-concepts}
temp <- issues %>%
  filter(ISSUE == "RESTATED_MATERIALLY", !is.na(CONCEPT)) %>%
  count(CONCEPT, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = top_n) %>%
  transmute(concept = paste0("`", CONCEPT, "`"), Facts = fmt(n))

if (nrow(temp) > 0) {
  knitr::kable(temp, align = "lr",
               col.names = c("The concept restated", "Facts"))
}
```

```{r worst-filings}
# Named so that a reader can go and look at them on EDGAR. The order is by
# errors first, which is the count that stops an analysis, and the codes are
# given so that a filing with many bad facts can be told from one with a
# single broken identity.
temp <- filing_state %>%
  filter(findings > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(errors), desc(findings)) %>%
  slice_head(n = top_n) %>%
  transmute(NAME = substr(NAME, 1, 28),

            Findings = fmt(findings),
            Errors = fmt(errors),

knitr::kable(temp, align = "lllrrl",
             col.names = c("Registrant", "Form", "Filed", "Findings",
                           "Errors", "What was found"))
```

## 4 What this report cannot say

```{r limits, results='asis'}
limits <- c(
  paste("**Whether a finding is a fault.** A check names a record that did",
        "not hold to a rule of this project. Several of the rules are held",
        "to by sound filings only most of the time: a registrant that",
        "presents no gross profit line has no income identity to test, a",
        "bank's revenue is interest income tagged elsewhere, and a filing",
        "whose period end is dragged past its filing date by a",
        "forward-looking fact is sound while the period end derived for it",
        "is not the period it is about. The catalogue in section 5 says for",
        "each check what a legitimate cause looks like, and no count in",
        "this report has one subtracted from it."),
  paste("**Whether a silence is a pass.** A check tests what a filing",
        "tagged. A filing that tagged neither side of an identity is not",
        "named by the identity check, and a filing that tags only",
        "cover-page facts is not named by any check that reads a figure.",
        "Both are counted here as filings with no finding of that check,",
        "which is why the `MISS_` checks are in the same table as the",
        "identities: they are the record of where the other checks had",
        "nothing to look at."),
  paste("**Whether the checks have run.** The table of issues holds the",
        "rows of the partitions the checks were last asked about. A year or",
        "a registrant the checks have not run over has no rows and is",
        "counted here as a part of the record with no findings. Section 1",
        "names the years this applies to; a report whose first table shows",
        "a year with no run cannot be read as a report on that year."),
  paste("**What a company file is.** The module reads the company facts the",
        "Commission publishes, which are the undimensioned numeric facts of",
        "a filing. The segmented figures, the text of the notes and the",
        "filing as filed are not in it. A check therefore tests the figures",
        "the Commission extracted, and a fault in that extraction and a",
        "fault in the filing look the same here; only the filing itself, on",
        "EDGAR, settles which it is."),
  paste("**Whether a figure is right.** An identity that holds says the",
        "figures a filing tagged are consistent with one another, not that",
        "they are the figures the accounts show, and a filing can tag a",
        "wrong number consistently in every statement. Nothing in the",
        "module re-runs the Commission's own validation either, and no",
        "finding here is a finding of the Commission."),
  paste("**What the severities are worth.** The three severities are this",
        "project's judgement of what a finding costs a reader of the data.",
        "They are not a classification the Commission publishes, and an",
        "analysis with different needs should read the codes rather than",
        "the severities: a warning that a figure was later restated decides",
        "whether a time series can be built at all, and an error in a cash",
        "flow identity does not touch a reader who only wants the balance",
        "sheet."),
  paste("**What happens next.** The module writes findings and changes",
        "nothing. No figure in the table of facts is corrected, no filing",
        "is set aside, and a filing that fails every check is read by the",
        "rest of the module exactly as one that passes. A pipeline that",
        "wants to act on a finding has to do so itself, which is what the",
        "table of issues is for."))

cat(paste(limits, collapse = "\n\n"))
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

## 5 The checks in full

```{r catalogue-intro, results='asis'}
cat("The catalogue the module ships, read from the same file the checks ",
    "read it from. Each entry says what the check finds, what a finding ",
    "means and what to do about it. The order is by severity.\n", sep = "")
```

```{r catalogue-full, results='asis'}
for (level in severities) {
  rows <- catalogue %>% filter(severity == level)
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) next
  heading <- switch(level,
                    error = "Errors",
                    warning = "Warnings",
                    info = "Notes")
  cat("\n### ", heading, "\n\n", sep = "")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(rows))) {
    found <- by_code %>% filter(ISSUE == rows$code[i])
    cat("**`", rows$code[i], "` — ", rows$title[i], ".** ",
        rows$meaning[i], " ",
        "*Found in ", fmt(found$affected), " of the ",
        fmt(found$denominator), " filings it is asked of",
        if (found$affected > 0)
          paste0(", ", fmt(found$findings), " findings") else "",
        ".* ",
        "*What to do:* ", rows$remedy[i], "\n\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```

### What was read

temp <- tibble(
  item = c("Silver layer",
           "Registrants",

           "Filings checked",

           "Facts the filings state",
           "Checks run",
           "Checks that fired",
           "Findings",
           "Of those, errors",
           "Of those, warnings",
           "Of those, notes",
           "Filings with a finding",
           "Annual reports free of errors",
           "Rows naming a filing no longer listed",
           "Checks last run",
           "Rendered on"),
  value = c(path_silver,
            fmt(n_registrants),
            period_range,
            fmt(n_filed),
            fmt(n_annual),
            fmt(sum(filing_state$FACTS, na.rm = TRUE)),
            fmt(n_checks),
            fmt(sum(by_code$affected > 0)),
            fmt(n_findings),
            fmt(n_errors),
            fmt(n_warnings),
            fmt(n_infos),
            fmt(sum(filing_state$findings > 0)),
            fmt(sum(rated$clean)),
            fmt(nrow(orphans)),
            if (checked_on[1] == checked_on[2])
              format(checked_on[1], "%d %B %Y") else
              paste(format(checked_on[1], "%d %b %Y"), "–",
                    format(checked_on[2], "%d %b %Y")),
            format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y")))

knitr::kable(temp, col.names = c("", ""), align = "lr")
```

### How to run the checks again

```{r rerun, results='asis'}
cat("The table of issues is rebuilt a partition at a time, and a partition ",
    "is rewritten as a whole when it is checked again, so a finding that ",
    "was fixed in the data leaves no row behind. From Python:\n\n",
    "```python\n",
    "from pyspark.sql import SparkSession\n",
    "from fincommons.secfiling.quality import ",
    "update_silver_secfiling_quality\n\n",
    "spark = SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()\n",
    "update_silver_secfiling_quality(spark, \"paths.yaml\",\n",
    "                                ciks=[\"0001045810\"])\n",
    "```\n\n",
    "`fincommons.dataquality.describe_check` turns a code into the ",
    "sentences printed in section 5, `issue_counts` counts the table by ",
    "code, and `with_issues` and `suppressed` join the findings onto the ",
    "figures so that a pipeline can act on them.\n", sep = "")
```

### Sources

```{r sources, results='asis'}
sources <- c(
  paste("**The filings and the facts.** The company facts the U.S.",
        "Securities and Exchange Commission publishes for each registrant",
        "at data.sec.gov, which carry the undimensioned numeric facts of",
        "every filing tagged in inline XBRL, each with the accession number",
        "of the filing it came from. The `secfiling` module reads them, by",
        "registrant or from the bulk archive of all of them."),
  paste("**The checks.** `fincommons.secfiling.quality`, with the machinery",
        "common to the regimes in `fincommons.dataquality` and the",
        "descriptions in `fincommons/data/dataquality_checks.csv`. All three",
        "are part of the open-source project fincommons and are the only",
        "source of the rules counted here."),
  paste("**The taxonomies.** The US GAAP and IFRS taxonomies name the",
        "concepts the checks look for, and the `dei` taxonomy the cover-page",
        "facts. A concept a registrant created for its own filing is not one",
        "the checks can read, which is what the `MISS_` checks record."))

cat(paste(sources, collapse = "\n\n"))
```
